leads.title: Indonesian Penal Code (KUHP) - 2022 revision, in force 2 January 2026
leads.documents: National legal status applicable in West Papua: sex outside marriage punishable up to 1 year on family complaint; spokesperson and Coordinating Minister Mahfud MD stated it does not criminalize private LGBTQ orientation, only same-sex sexual violence/rape of minors and public immoral acts; draft Art.421(1) on same-sex obscenity in public (1.5 years).
leads.detail: No URL visible in excerpt; cited as December 2022 Parliament bill, Art.248 adultery, Art.285 rape, Art.292 child abuse, Art.421(1) obscenity, effective date 2 January 2026

leads.title: Qanun Jinayat - Aceh Sharia Criminal Code (2014)
leads.documents: Regional exception showing West Papua is NOT under Sharia criminalization: in Aceh consensual adult same-sex acts punishable by up to 100 lashes or up to 100 months imprisonment; used for public canings including 2017 case of 2 gay men aged 20 and 23, and Aug 2025 caning for kissing.
leads.detail: No URL visible in excerpt; cited as 2014 Qanun Jinayat, 100 lashes / 100 months, Aceh special autonomous status

leads.title: Constitutional Court of Indonesia - 5-4 Ruling 14 December 2017
leads.documents: Rejected Family Love Alliance petition to erase 'underage' from Art.292 to criminalize all same-sex conduct; held criminalization is legislature matter, preserving national legality of private consensual adult same-sex activity relevant to West Papua.
leads.detail: No URL visible in excerpt; cited as 14 December 2017, 5-4 decision, petition on KUHP Arts.248, 285, 292

leads.title: Constitution of Indonesia + Human Rights Law No.39/1999
leads.documents: Rights machinery applicable in West Papua: Constitution guarantees equality before law, humane workplace treatment, assembly/association but no explicit SOGI mention; theoretical employment anti-discrimination protection via Constitution and Law No.39/1999.
leads.detail: No URL visible in excerpt; cited as constitutional equality guarantees and Human Rights Law (No.39/1999)

leads.title: Head of National Police Regulation No.8 of 2009 + 2015 hate-speech circular
leads.documents: Enforcement/protection machinery: police duty to protect special rights of minority groups including sexual orientation, and to process hate speech related to sexual orientation and gender identity.
leads.detail: No URL visible in excerpt; cited as Regulation of the Head of National Police No.8 of 2009 and 2015 circular letter

leads.title: Law Against Pornography and Pornoaction (2006)
leads.documents: Main enforcement tool used nationally including West Papua for raids on gay parties/saunas: prohibits writing/audio-visual suggesting same-sex sexual relations, up to 7 years; cited for Nov 2016 FPI-tipped raid, May 2017 arrests of 141 and 144 in Jakarta, Oct 2017 arrest of 51, 2025 villa/hotel raids.
leads.detail: No URL visible in excerpt; cited as 2006 Law, fine or up to seven years imprisonment

leads.title: Ministry of Home Affairs - Transgender ID (KTP) outreach since June 2021
leads.documents: Directly names Papua: transgender residents of Papua among those issued Kartu Tanda Penduduk and family register access; only male/female descriptors, birth gender retained unless court recognition after surgery; critical for trans visitor ID/police interaction.
leads.detail: No URL visible in excerpt; cited as June 2021 program covering Banten, West Java, Central Java, East Java, North Sumatra, South Sumatra, South Sulawesi, Lampung, and Papua

leads.title: Judicial precedent on legal gender change - Vivian Rubiyanti Iskandar case
leads.documents: Trans legal status rule: allowed to change legal gender on official documents after sex reassignment surgery and judge approval, then able to marry opposite legal gender; contrasts with MUI ruling that trans must live as birth gender.
leads.detail: No URL visible in excerpt; cited as Vivian Rubiyanti Iskandar first legally recognized trans woman, plus Dorce Gamalama and Aprilio Manganang 2021 cases

leads.title: Semarang State Administrative Court - TT police dismissal case + National Commission on Human Rights (Komnas HAM)
leads.documents: Discrimination remedy machinery: 30-year-old brigadier TT fired for being gay filed 2019 lawsuit and Komnas HAM complaint; court rejected May 2019 on procedural grounds; Attorney General's Office rescinded LGBTQ-exclusion job ad after Komnas HAM advice.
leads.detail: No URL visible in excerpt; cited as March 2019 filing, May 2019 rejection, Central Java Police, Yuli Retoblaut 2007 Komnas HAM commissioner bid

leads.title: Pew Research Center - 2025 and 2023 surveys
leads.documents: Social climate data for safety dossier: 93% in 2025 label homosexuality morally unacceptable (comparable Nigeria 96%); 95% in 2023 oppose same-sex marriage; documents high stigma despite legality.
leads.detail: No URL visible in excerpt; cited as Pew Research Center 2025 data and 2023 estimate
